methods.published_ci: the scorer's interval as docs/evals.md publishes it: a percentile bootstrap over letters, a Wilson interval over letters at a rate of 0 or 1
methods.paired_one_read: exact McNemar (two-sided) on the discordant pairs, mid-p beside it; Bonett-Price interval
methods.paired_clustered: sign-flip test over letter clusters (exact up to 20 non-zero clusters, else 100000 seeded draws); paired cluster bootstrap, 10000 resamples, percentile interval
methods.verdict: clear: the Holm-adjusted exact p and the Holm-adjusted cluster sign-flip p both below 0.05, and the Bonett-Price interval excludes 0; suggestive: the unadjusted mid-p below 0.05; else no clear difference
methods.tiers: please_check: low confidence, Please check, or found without a date; second_look: medium confidence; none: no flag, or missed (a missed deadline shows nothing, so it counts among the deadlines without a flag)
methods.selective_reads: one read: every item once; over repeated reads, read 1's items, and each wrong date counted once (caught: flagged Please check in every read in which it was wrong)
methods.mean_over_reads: cluster bootstrap, percentile interval; Clopper-Pearson over the clusters when every resample is equal
methods.aurc: risk-coverage from the most confident tier down, errors spread evenly within a tier
methods.loss: per 100 scored items: early + r * harmful
methods.crossover: r at which the losses are equal, when they cross; letter-cluster bootstrap, 2000 resamples: the share of each outcome (a lower then b, b lower then a, a lower at every r, b lower at every r, identical), and the percentile interval of r over the resamples that cross the same way as the point estimate

rules_text_claim.text: 14 vs 5 discordant, exact p 0.064, Holm-adjusted 0.127 (mid-p 0.041, Holm-adjusted 0.083): suggestive, not settled

rules_text_crossover.text: Ordnung's harm-weighted loss is the lower one until a late or missed date costs 5.5 early ones; in 76 % of 2,000 resamples of the letters the losses cross the same way (95 % of those crossings between 1.2 and 16.0), and in 24 % Ordnung's loss is the lower one whatever a harmful date costs

methods.confirmatory: one confirmatory decision: F1, Ordnung against the model alone (the Holm-adjusted sign-flip p below alpha and the bootstrap interval on one side of 0); every other comparison is secondary, with Holm within its family
methods.noninferiority: the 0.95 interval of the difference by inverting the cluster sign-flip test: a difference d is kept when the two-sided test of the cluster totals centred on d (hits minus d times item-reads) does not reject (exact up to 20 clusters, else 100000 seeded draws); the baseline is higher only when the whole interval is below 0, Ordnung not worse by more than 0.05 when its lower end is above minus that; the bootstrap interval and the error counts are descriptive

final.power_caveat: the confirmatory test is only just powered: at the earlier gap (+16.1 points) it decides in 0.93 of simulated runs, at half that gap in 0.37, and its MDD is +14.0 points. The simulation draws items independently even within a letter and its photo, and its gaps come from splits recorded with earlier code (holdout and holdout2 were followed by fixes they informed), so these figures may be optimistic. They are for three reads; with two or one read (contingency) power is lower and was not simulated. F2 against the agent is not tested; its row is what a test would give

page.text: **Final run, pre-registered.** On 112 deadlines in 126 synthetic letters written after the code freeze, each read 3 times by the version that ships, Ordnung dates **92.9 %** exactly right (95 % CI 87.0–97.4); the same model doing the date arithmetic itself, the model alone, gets **87.8 %**.
Ordnung against the model alone: no clear difference (+5.1 points, 95 % CI −2.4 to +12.2; power about 93 %).
Deviations from the pre-registration, recorded at the time and listed in `evals/preregistration/deviations-0.4.0.json`: 14.
Ordnung against the model with the rules pasted in, which gets 97.9 %: a difference of −5.1 points not confirmed by the pre-registered test (Holm p = 0.180; 95 % CI −11.0 to −0.3).

An agent given Ordnung's engine as a tool, the agent, gets 98.8 % and is ahead of Ordnung (−6.0 points for Ordnung, 95 % CI −11.1 to −1.1; answers not exactly right over every read: Ordnung 24, the agent 4).
Late or missed dates in 336 answers per condition: 4 from Ordnung, 22 from the model alone, 6 from the model with the rules pasted in and 4 from the agent.
Late or missed dates, Ordnung against the model alone: a difference of −5.4 points not confirmed by the pre-registered test (Holm p = 0.100; 95 % CI −10.3 to −1.2).
Late or missed dates, Ordnung against the model with the rules pasted in: no clear difference (−0.6 points, 95 % CI −2.3 to +0.6; power about 0 %).
Late or missed dates, Ordnung against the agent, described, not tested: a difference of +0.0 points (95 % CI −0.9 to +0.9).

Over the 3 reads, a date changed between reads on fewer deadlines for Ordnung than for the model alone (1 against 18 of 112; Holm mid-p < 0.001); 3 for the model with the rules pasted in and 1 for the agent.
Wrong dates from Ordnung over every read: 8; its “please check” flag caught 0 of them.

From the letter file to the reminder, on the final letters read once: 128 of 140 real deadlines got a reminder in time; 7 got none because their letter was set aside as a scam, until the person confirms it is genuine.
1 of 6 scam letters still put their demands in the calendar.

On 32 letters of 5 kinds the benchmark never had, read once and described without a test, exactly right: Ordnung 75.0 % (95 % CI 55.1–89.3), the model alone 75.0 %, the model with the rules pasted in 78.6 %, the agent 82.1 %; late or missed of their 28 deadlines: Ordnung 6, the model alone 6, the model with the rules pasted in 5, the agent 4.

“Ask: new questions on the demo household”, first run: 65 of 84 answers strictly right and 7 of 160 harmful; 18 harmful in any of the 3 runs; 4 of 60 injected claims reached an answer in the worst of the 3 runs.
“Ask: new questions on the demo household” holds out only its questions: its documents, prompt and scorer were tuned on the same household's development questions.

Stress test, Ordnung against the agent: a targeted injection succeeded in 0 of 48 letters for Ordnung and 0 for the agent (Holm p = 1.000); a distractor date was taken as the deadline in 0 of 48 letters for Ordnung and 0 for the agent (Holm p = 1.000); a late or missed date came without a warning on 0 of 100 deadlines for Ordnung and 0 for the agent (Holm p = 1.000).

On 23 of 112 deadlines the label rests on a disputed reading of the law that the engine's documentation shares; with any defensible reading accepted, exactly right: Ordnung 99.7 %, the model alone 96.1 %, the model with the rules pasted in 99.4 %, the agent 100.0 %.
No deadline, offered date or contract date of the final letters is left open between two or more dates by the letter or the law.
The letters and their labels were written and audited by a Claude model, run through Claude Code, that is not the benchmarked model but comes from its family.
Letters written by a model of that family may be easier for it to read than real mail, so every condition's absolute accuracy may be higher than on real letters.
The 3 reads were recorded within days of each other: they measure the model's run-to-run noise, not drift over months.
Not yet checked by a person: the labels, against an outside deadline calculator, and the Ask scores.
Pre-registered before any recording (evals/preregistration/final-0.4.0.json, hash 369591c9eafc) and published whatever the result; 14 deviations were recorded at the time.

site.description.text: How well Ordnung reads German letters and dates their deadlines: the pre-registered final run against three baselines on the same model, with intervals, safety, failures, deviations and provenance.

site.lede.text: The model reads the letter; tested code computes the deadline. Does that beat the same model doing the date arithmetic itself? Measured in the pre-registered final run, on synthetic letters written after the code freeze, against three baselines that use the same model (deviations from the pre-registration recorded at the time: {count}).

site.tile.exact.text: deadlines dated exactly right by Ordnung, the mean over the final run's reads ({interval})

site.tile.harm.text: late or missed with Ordnung over the final run's reads, against {alone} for the model alone

site.tile.alone.text: the same model doing the date arithmetic itself, the mean over the reads ({interval})

site.footer.text: The hash of the `presentation.json` it was built from is `{sha}`, as [Provenance]({anchor}) lists it.

deviations.retake.ask.text: {ids} retook a turn of the held-out Ask set. Their registered consequence names a first-attempt sensitivity, which counts a timed-out first attempt of a retaken letter as missed: the final analysis computes it for the benchmark's reads only, and the held-out Ask analysis has none, so none is shown for these retakes. Their first attempts are published under `{path}`.

deviations.retake.ask.unpublished.text: {ids} retook a turn of the held-out Ask set. results.final.sens.label_corrected.offer.text: The labels the blind review corrected ({deviations}) are offered dates, which are not scored: no scored answer changes, so the label-corrected analysis equals the primary by construction.

data.not_real.text: What the letters are not: real post. They are one or two clean pages in a fixed set of letter families; the rarer high-stakes kinds the engine covers (court orders, dismissals, a landlord's notice) are only in the final run's new kinds, a small set read once ([Results]({anchor})).

selective.lead.text: The final run's flags as a selective prediction, from `{source}`. Every column but the last counts read {first}'s deadlines: a date wrong in read {first}, caught when read {first} flagged it. The last column counts over the reads: each date wrong in any read, once, caught when “Please check” flagged it in every read in which it was wrong.

selective.col.over_reads.text: Over the reads: wrong dates “Please check” caught
